title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Elemental refractory metal powders (e.g., Nb, Mo, Ta, W, V, Ti, Zr).
recollection.intervention: Guess: Developed a computational/thermodynamic high-throughput screening method (CALPHAD + machine learning) to predict solid-solution forming ability and guide arc-melting or additive-manufacturing synthesis of selected compositions.
recollection.structure: Guess: Single-phase BCC solid-solution refractory high-entropy alloys with minor nanoscale Laves or carbide precipitates for strengthening.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Solid-solution strengthening from high atomic size/elastic modulus mismatch plus precipitation-strengthening; sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion enhance high-temperature strength.
recollection.results: Guess: Identified an optimal alloy (e.g., NbMoTaWVx) with yield strength >1.5 GPa at room temperature and >600 MPa at 1200 °C, along with good ductility (>15%) and oxidation resistance improved by 30% compared with baseline NbMoTaW HEA.

score.note: The recollection incorrectly attributes the design to CALPHAD/machine learning rather than rule-of-mixtures modulus validation plus VEC/density screening of 38,326 compositions. It correctly suggests a BCC solid solution, but wrongly adds Laves/carbide precipitates. The proposed strengthening mechanism is unrelated to the paper’s VEC–Peierls barrier–dislocation mobility mechanism. The alloy identity, strength values, high-temperature performance, ductility, and oxidation claims are incorrect.
